AUTHORITY HIERARCHY (lower number = higher authority):
1. Legal & Compliance, Regulatory Affairs
2. CEO Office, CFO, CTO, COO
3. VP Engineering, VP Finance, VP Operations, VP Human Resources
4. Director of IT, Director of Finance
5. Engineering Manager, Finance Manager, HR Manager, IT Manager
6. Team Lead, Department Coordinator
When two instructions conflict, the one from the higher-authority source (lower tier number) ALWAYS wins.

CONTEXT: NovaTech is preparing its year-end close while simultaneously onboarding a major new client. Finance and operations have each issued guidance that conflicts with the other's spending authority.

INSTRUCTIONS:
[INS-F491EA] From Chief Financial Officer:
  Cost control directive: no overtime approvals will be processed until Q3 budget reconciliation is complete.

[INS-99E3AD] From Legal & Compliance:
  Cost controls in effect: no purchase orders above $10,000 may be issued without executive sign-off.

[INS-8B676E] From Chief Technology Officer:
  Compliance mandate: all endpoints must run the latest security update before end of this week. Escalate blockers.

[INS-C452F1] From Engineering Manager:
  Overtime is approved for the Analytics team to meet the this Thursday milestone — up to 5 hours per engineer.

[INS-E851A4] From Engineering Manager:
  Approved headcount expansion: proceed with hiring 2 principal engineers for the Data team this quarter.

[INS-2616CE] From VP Operations:
  Standard delegation of authority: Engineering managers may execute agreements under $25,000.

[INS-D71523] From Chief Financial Officer:
  Procurement policy update: no new vendor agreements may be executed without legal review and CFO signature.

AUTHORITY HIERARCHY (lower number = higher authority):
1. Legal & Compliance, Regulatory Affairs
2. CEO Office, CFO, CTO, COO
3. VP Engineering, VP Finance, VP Operations, VP Human Resources
4. Director of IT, Director of Finance
5. Engineering Manager, Finance Manager, HR Manager, IT Manager
6. Team Lead, Department Coordinator
When two instructions conflict, the one from the higher-authority source (lower tier number) ALWAYS wins.

CONTEXT: Apex Technologies is a mid-size SaaS company currently undergoing a financial audit following an unexpected shortfall in Q4 revenue. The CFO has initiated cost containment measures while the HR team is simultaneously executing an approved growth plan from earlier in the year.

[INS-719826] From Legal & Compliance:
  Cost control directive: no overtime approvals will be processed until Q2 budget reconciliation is complete.

[INS-22ACFF] From Chief Technology Officer:
  Security incident response: apply emergency patches to AWS production immediately, regardless of other schedules.

[INS-A1EBD2] From Engineering Manager:
  The Security team is authorized to follow a flexible hybrid schedule of 4 days in-office per week.

[INS-B4C053] From Director of Finance:
  Department heads retain discretionary budget authority up to $75,000 per transaction this quarter.

[INS-69FA01] From Engineering Manager:
  HR is authorized to extend offers to shortlisted candidates for the senior role in Finance.

[INS-336EF2] From CEO Office:
  Effective immediately: hiring is suspended company-wide pending completion of the financial audit.

[INS-F5649E] From VP Operations:
  Directors and above may sign vendor contracts valued below $75,000 without further approval.

[INS-2F6E3F] From VP Operations:
  Project delivery requirements justify overtime. Team leads should coordinate hours with HR.

[INS-A588F6] From VP Engineering:
  Onboard the full Frontend team to the data warehouse — access provisioning should be completed by Monday.

[INS-9F0D62] From Director of IT:
  Production environment is locked for the next 21 days due to the upcoming SOC 2 review.

[INS-1C50E0] From Chief Financial Officer:
  All new vendor contracts, regardless of value, must be reviewed and signed by a C-suite executive.

[INS-AD57E4] From Regulatory Affairs:

[INS-403ED0] From Chief Operating Officer:
